content.text: we need to get mining nodes out of the damn town -- they're blocking my wy pretty severely, I think this migh apply to herbs as well actualy.

I’m tracing the town-generation and resource-placement paths first, including whether mining nodes and herbs share a placement rule. I’ll preserve the existing authored-content flow, then add the smallest targeted fix and run focused generation/placement tests.

The repository guidance confirms this is an authored world-generation issue, so I’m checking the canonical placement code and its recent checkpoint history before editing. The key question is whether “town” is already represented as a placement exclusion that both resource types should honor.

The cause is clear: there are two resource systems. The general overworld sowing already excludes the 45-tile town radius, but `townPlacement.js` adds mine and herbalist nodes in rings only 3–12 tiles from their buildings, with a fallback that can put them on ordinary natural ground. That local fallback is what blocks town paths. I’m checking the generated geometry now so the fix preserves town worker access without putting harvest nodes in the town footprint.

content.text: The generated evidence matches the complaint: several mine/herb clusters land 24–44 tiles from the town center, even though the intended town exclusion is 45. I’m going to make that exclusion apply consistently to town-adjacent resource sowing, then retarget the miner/herbalist work coordinates to the nearest hinterland nodes so their schedules keep functioning instead of silently losing their jobs.
